evidence_refs: Python shlex and shell injection guidance
explanation: Passing user-controlled text into a shell command string can allow shell interpretation and command injection. Supplying an argument list avoids shell parsing in the common case.
safety_notes: Avoid shell=True unless it is strictly required and reviewed. Validate paths and user input before invoking subprocesses.
title: Unsafe subprocess shell=True with user input
verification_steps: Check that arguments are passed as a list, not a shell string.
Confirm shell=True is not used for untrusted input.
Review whether path validation is needed before execution.

corrected_pattern: Check whether the target path exists, require explicit overwrite intent, and prefer a temporary file or backup before replacing the original file.
evidence_refs: safe write and backup workflow guidance
explanation: Opening a file in write mode can truncate existing content immediately. Safer workflows make overwrite intent explicit and reduce silent data loss.
safety_notes: Avoid silent overwrite of existing files. Use a temp file, backup, or explicit confirmation step for destructive writes.
title: Unsafe file overwrite without explicit intent
unsafe_or_wrong_pattern: open(path, "w") without checking whether the file exists or whether overwrite is intended
verification_steps: Check whether the target path already exists.
Review whether overwrite confirmation, backup, or temp-file replacement is required.
Confirm the workflow documents possible data-loss impact.

corrected_pattern: python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pip install package
evidence_refs: Debian and Ubuntu externally managed Python guidance
explanation: Installing packages globally into a system-managed Python can break distribution tooling or violate externally managed environment rules. A virtual environment keeps project dependencies isolated.
safety_notes: Avoid sudo pip install for system Python. Prefer venv for project dependencies and consider pipx for standalone CLI tools.
title: Unsafe global pip install on externally managed Python
unsafe_or_wrong_pattern: sudo pip install package or pip install globally on an externally managed system Python
verification_steps: Check whether the system Python is externally managed.
Confirm the workflow uses venv or pipx instead of global pip.
Verify installation guidance does not require modifying system Python.
